name: Cloudflare Documentation MCP
description: Search Cloudflare developer documentation through its public documentation server.
reason: Useful when evaluating Workers, R2 photo storage, caching, or deployment options for SiteMonitor. Public documentation access does not require a Cloudflare account.

name: Linear MCP
description: Find and manage Linear issues, projects, and comments from a coding agent.
reason: An optional planning connection if your team uses Linear for estate work or development tasks. Your existing GitHub MCP may already cover your issue-tracking needs.

name: Cloudflare API MCP
description: Search and call Cloudflare API endpoints, and look up its developer documentation.
reason: Consider this if you deploy through Cloudflare and want agents to inspect or manage Workers, R2, and DNS. It needs a Cloudflare account with the relevant permissions.

name: Brave Search MCP
description: Official Brave integration for web, news, image, video, and other search tools.
reason: An alternative search provider when Brave's search results or filters suit a task. Exa and Perplexity are already installed, so add this only if you want another provider. Requires a Brave Search API key.

name: Docker MCP Gateway
description: Run and route containerized MCP servers through Docker's gateway and profiles.
reason: Optional if you want a Docker-based MCP runtime shared by multiple coding agents. Requires Docker Desktop with MCP Toolkit, or Docker Engine with the gateway installed; it is not a general-purpose Docker administration server.

name: canvas-design
description: Create static visual compositions as PNG or PDF files.
reason: Adds a workflow for posters, visual handover material, and presentation graphics alongside your existing UI-design and document skills.

name: internal-comms
description: Draft structured status reports, leadership updates, FAQs, and incident communications.
reason: Useful for turning SiteMonitor progress, decisions, and operational incidents into clear updates for estate owners and office staff.

name: theme-factory
description: Apply coordinated color and font themes to slides, documents, and HTML artifacts.
reason: An optional way to keep owner reports and presentation artifacts visually consistent. Your existing design-system and frontend skills already cover much of the application styling work.

name: web-artifacts-builder
description: Build and bundle multi-component React and Tailwind prototypes into a single HTML artifact.
reason: Useful for isolated interactive demonstrations and stakeholder prototypes. Its React toolchain is separate from SiteMonitor's Rust/Dioxus application and should be used only when that prototype format is wanted.

name: algorithmic-art
description: Create generative p5.js artwork with seeded randomness and interactive parameters.
reason: An optional creative tool for original visual assets and motion studies. It is a specialist art workflow rather than a requirement for the monitoring application.

name: claude-api
description: Reference workflows for building applications with the Claude API and Anthropic SDKs.
reason: Consider this only if you add Claude-powered functionality to an application. It is provider-specific, and actually calling Claude requires API access; it is not needed just to use your coding agents.
